meta.date: The practice of the church, written out by Moroni after AD 400
meta.unit: The manner of administering the wine (Moroni 5)
principles: A second prayer built on the first
Blood named where the body had been
A promise that follows one commitment instead of three

world_behind.title: The chapter has no frame beyond a line
world_behind.text: Verse 1 gives the heading and the cup, and verse 2 is the prayer. Moroni 4:1 and 2 spend two verses on who administered and how they knelt before reaching the words; this chapter drops all of it and keeps only the form.

world_behind.title: A cup is named
world_behind.text: Verse 1 says they took the cup.

world_behind.title: The wording follows Moroni 4 closely
world_behind.text: The address, the asking in the name of the Son, and the closing promise are the same.

world_behind.title: The element changes
world_behind.text: Wine stands where bread stood and blood where the body stood. 3 Nephi 18:8 and 9 records the wine being given and drunk on the day of the visit, and 3 Nephi 20:5 has it given again without anyone having brought any.

world_behind.title: A clause is added
world_behind.text: Verse 2 says the blood was shed for them, and Moroni 4:3 has no counterpart clause for the body. 3 Nephi 18:11 says whoso drinketh of this wine drinketh of my blood to his soul, which is where both prayers take their language from.

world_behind.title: Two commitments drop out
world_behind.text: The wine prayer carries neither the willingness to take the name nor the keeping of commandments that Moroni 4:3 asks for, and it keeps the promise of the Spirit unchanged. What is common to both forms is remembrance and the Spirit.

world_behind.title: The promise loses a word
world_behind.text: Verse 2 says they may have his Spirit, where Moroni 4:3 says always have it.

words.text: Handing something out in an official capacity. Treated at Moroni 4:1. The two headings are the only places the record uses it of this ordinance.
The vessel the wine is taken from. The record uses the word ten times and the King James Bible sixty-eight. Moroni 4 names no vessel for the bread.
The drink used. Treated at 3 Nephi 18:8. It appears forty times in the record and two hundred and thirty-one in the King James Bible.
To set apart for a holy use. Treated at Moroni 4:3. The word carries across from the bread prayer unchanged.
The people themselves, as distinct from their bodies. It appears ninety-one times in the record, and the King James Bible seventy-eight.
To take in liquid. The record uses the word thirty-one times and the King James Bible three hundred and sixty-nine. Verse 2 puts it where Moroni 4:3 has eat.
Poured out. The word turns up nineteen times here, and the King James Bible fifty-two. Verse 2 adds it to a sentence the bread prayer leaves shorter.

phrases.term: The manner of administering the wine
phrases.text: The heading, four words shorter than the one in Moroni 4. The frame is cut down because the reader already has it.

phrases.term: Behold, they took the cup, and said
phrases.text: The whole of the narrative in this chapter. One gesture and one verb of speech.

phrases.term: O God, the Eternal Father, we ask thee, in the name of thy Son
phrases.text: The address, carried over word for word. Only a comma moves.

phrases.term: To bless and sanctify this wine to the souls of all those who drink of it
phrases.text: The request, with two words changed. Wine replaces bread and drink replaces partake.

phrases.term: That they may do it in remembrance of the blood of thy Son
phrases.text: The purpose. Blood stands where the body stood in Moroni 4:3.
The clause with no counterpart in the bread prayer. It says what the blood was for.

phrases.term: That they may witness unto thee, O God, the Eternal Father
phrases.text: The address repeated inside the prayer. Both prayers do this at the same point.

phrases.term: That they do always remember him
phrases.text: The one thing witnessed here. Moroni 4:3 has three, and this has the middle one.

phrases.term: That they may have his Spirit to be with them
phrases.text: The closing promise. The word always, which stands in Moroni 4:3, is absent.
The close of the second form. Moroni gives both prayers entire and comments on neither.

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: Twelve words of heading
verses.text: The wine gets no elders and priests, no appeal to the commandments of Christ, no kneeling — only "Behold, they took the cup, and said." Moroni 4:1 spent forty-three words certifying the form. It is certified once and not again.

verses.label: v. 2
verses.title: What the second prayer drops
verses.text: Set beside Moroni 4:3, this is seventy-eight words to ninety-one, and the cuts fall together. The bread asks that they be "willing to take upon them the name of thy Son" and that they "keep his commandments"; the wine asks neither. The bread's "always have his Spirit" loses its always. What the wine adds is the one thing the bread never says: the blood "which was shed for them."

chapter.title: The chapter assumes Moroni 4
chapter.text: Verse 1 drops the frame about elders, priests, and kneeling, since the previous page has it.

chapter.title: The address is identical
chapter.text: Verse 2 opens with the same eight words the bread prayer opens with.

chapter.title: The element governs the verbs
chapter.text: The two prayers are nearly identical and the differences are confined to the element and its verbs. Moroni 4:3 has bread with "eat," "partake," and "eat in remembrance of the body of thy Son." Moroni 5:2 has wine with "drink," "drink it," and "do it in remembrance of the blood of thy Son." The wine prayer is also shorter: it drops the clause about taking the name of the Son and the clause about keeping his commandments, both of which stand in the bread prayer. Two fixed forms, differing in one element and two clauses.

chapter.title: A reason is added
chapter.text: Verse 2 names the shedding of blood on their behalf, and the bread prayer says nothing about what the body was for.

chapter.title: Two of the three commitments drop away
chapter.text: Willingness to take the name and keeping the commandments are absent here.

chapter.title: What remains is the middle one
chapter.text: Verse 2 keeps always remembering him, which both prayers share.

chapter.title: The promise is shorter by one word
chapter.text: Moroni 4:3 has always have his Spirit, and verse 2 has have his Spirit.

chapter.title: Moroni supplies both and explains neither
chapter.text: The two chapters run back to back with no comment on the differences.

applications.title: The cup is taken before anything is said
applications.text: The chapter opens with them taking the cup, and the words come after. The physical act belongs to the ordinance rather than framing it.

applications.title: Say the second thing as carefully as the first
applications.text: The wine prayer is not a shortened repeat; it is its own form.

applications.title: Notice what a text adds
applications.text: The clause saying the blood was shed for them has no counterpart in Moroni 4:3.

applications.title: Notice what a text drops
applications.text: Two commitments from Moroni 4 do not appear, and the promise still stands.

applications.title: One promise, word for word the same
applications.text: The wine prayer asks for less and still closes with having his Spirit to be with them. What survives unchanged across two forms is generally the part that carries the weight.

applications.title: Let remembering be enough sometimes
applications.text: This prayer asks for one thing and attaches the Spirit to it.

questions.text: What have I inherited a form for and never examined?
What does the blood having been shed for me change today?
Do I always remember him, in the plain sense of the words?
Which of these two prayers do I actually listen to?
What am I asking to be sanctified to my soul?
Where do I want his Spirit with me this week?
What would I notice if I heard these words for the first time?

entries.head: Moro. 4:3

anchor.quote: to bless and sanctify this wine to the souls of all those who drink of it

entries.reason: the bread prayer, with two words changed

targets.quote: to bless and sanctify this bread to the souls of all those who partake of it;
targets.verse_text: O God, the Eternal Father, we ask thee in the name of thy Son, Jesus Christ, to bless and sanctify this bread to the souls of all those who partake of it; that they may eat in remembrance of the body of thy Son, and witness unto thee, O God, the Eternal Father, that they are willing to take upon them the name of thy Son, and always remember him, and keep his commandments which he hath given them, that they may always have his Spirit to be with them. Amen.
targets.markdown: O God, the Eternal Father, we ask thee in the name of thy Son, Jesus Christ, **to bless and sanctify this bread to the souls of all those who partake of it**; that they may eat in remembrance of the body of thy Son, and witness unto thee, O God, the Eternal Father, that they are willing to take upon them the name of thy Son, and always remember him, and keep his commandments which he hath given them, that they may always have his Spirit to be with them. Amen.
